title: The Silent Choir
premise: Rosalind Winterbourne, the last active courier of the Wayfarers' Guild, finds tonight's date inscribed in the Ash Codex, a book of prophecies sealed a century ago by a guildmaster who vanished. The prophecy names them as the Silent Choir's conductor: the one who can wake the memories sleeping in the dragon-fire that powers King Aldous's crown. But the thing wearing the crown is a memory-eater called the Regent, which has been consuming the king's identity and the kingdom's history to keep itself alive. Rosalind must gather the scattered choir—survivors whose songs hold fragments of true memory—and carry them through Thornfell to the dying dragon beneath the palace, unbinding Aldous and burning the Regent away, though the price is the guild's own memory of Rosalind, leaving them finally seen by a kingdom that will never know their name.
about_author: I. M. Voss is a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three libraries that officially never existed. They write fantasy from a narrowboat on an unnamed river, and refuse to confirm which memories in their books are borrowed.

chapters.title: The Date That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Delivering contraband candles through Thornfell, they shelter in the ruined Guildhouse and find tonight's date freshly inked in the century-sealed Ash Codex. The beat: unease—the invisible life they've built has a crack in it.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Vanished
chapters.summary: Rosalind deciphers the Codex's first page: the Wayfarers were founded to carry memories, not goods, and a 'Silent Choir' was meant to sing them back. Their guildmaster's name is the last entry before the blank. Beat: reluctant curiosity overriding fear.

chapters.title: The Crown at Dinner
chapters.summary: Rosalind, posing as a wine merchant, witnesses King Aldous at a feast—charming, hollow-eyed, repeating a courtier's joke word for word from an hour before. The crown seems to drink the lamplight. Beat: cold recognition that the prophecy's villain is real.

chapters.title: What the Guild Knew
chapters.summary: Rosalind visits Maren Ostwick, the guild's last elder, now a lockkeeper gone half-blind. Maren confirms the Choir's existence and warns: 'The Regent eats what remembers you. Sing, and it finds you.' Beat: inheritance as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: First Verse
chapters.summary: Rosalind discovers they can hear memory-songs in old objects—a smuggler's coin hums with its owner's last morning. When they hum back, the Regent's attention brushes the mountains like weather. Beat: wonder curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: The Hunter in the Pass
chapters.summary: A crown agent called Serle, face oddly forgettable, begins tracking the 'unlicensed singer.' Rosalind loses him only by burning a memory of their mother's face from a locket as a decoy. Beat: first true cost; grief and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: Chorister Found
chapters.summary: In a mining town, Rosalind finds Tam Broadhurst, a deaf stonemason who feels memory-songs as vibration and has hidden his gift for years. He refuses—until the Regent's agents erase his late wife from every record but his hands. Beat: grief as recruitment.

chapters.title: Two Voices
chapters.summary: Tam and Rosalind test singing together; their harmonies unlock a vault of guild memory beneath a chapel, revealing the Codex was written by guildmaster Ede Voss—who walked into the palace a century ago and never came out. Beat: awe, and the first hint the author is kin.

chapters.title: The Regent's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV shift: the Regent, wearing Aldous, gently erases a dying queen's pain as a mercy, then eats the memory of her. It believes it is saving people from grief. Beat: chilling sympathy for the antagonist.

chapters.title: Serle's Offer
chapters.summary: Serle corners Rosalind: he was a chorister once, before the Regent took his memories and left him only obedience. He offers safe passage to the palace if they surrender the Codex. Beat: temptation of an easy ending.

chapters.title: The Third Voice Is a Liar
chapters.summary: A charming balladeer, Wren, claims chorister lineage and joins them—Rosalind suspects her songs are too polished. Tam's vibrations confirm: her memory-songs are manufactured. Beat: paranoia inside the found family.

chapters.title: Thornfell in Winter
chapters.summary: The three cross the high passes as the Regent's agents seal the roads. A blizzard forces them into a smuggler's cave where Rosalind's childhood is carved into the walls—someone preserved their memories here, deliberately. Beat: vulnerability; who protected them, and why?

chapters.title: Ede's Cave
chapters.summary: Deciphering the carvings, they learn Ede Voss hid Rosalind's family line from the Regent for generations: the Wintervournes are the Choir's hereditary conductors. Rosalind was raised invisible on purpose. Beat: anger at the guild's lies, then understanding.

chapters.title: The Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: From a ridge, Rosalind sees the palace's dragon-fire beacon dim for the first time in living memory. The dragon below is dying, and with it the anchor holding the Regent in the crown. Beat: the clock becomes audible.

chapters.title: Wren's True Verse
chapters.summary: Cornered, Wren confesses: she's the Regent's creation, a memory given flesh, sent to lead them astray—but singing with the Choir has given her a self that doesn't want to obey. Beat: identity theme made flesh; trust as an act, not a fact.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot
chapters.summary: In the capital, entire districts have forgotten their own names; the Regent is feeding faster to survive the dragon's death. Rosalind's guild insignia gets them shelter from strangers who feel they owe Wayfarers something they can't recall. Beat: the guild's legacy as quiet, living grace.

chapters.title: Palace of Echoes
chapters.summary: Using Serle's old routes, they enter the palace's memory-vaults: shelves of glass vials, each a stolen life. Rosalind finds a vial labeled with their own name. Beat: dread—they have already been eaten, once.

chapters.title: The Missing Year
chapters.summary: Rosalind opens the vial against Maren's advice and recovers a year they never knew they'd lost: they met Aldous, the real king, as a child; he begged them to remember him if he ever stopped being himself. Beat: devastating recontextualization of the whole quest.

chapters.title: Aldous, Briefly
chapters.summary: A chance corridor encounter: the king's true self surfaces for eleven seconds, recognizes Rosalind, and says 'Sing it back to me' before the Regent slams shut like a door. Beat: hope with a time limit.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Verse
chapters.summary: Maren arrives, having walked from the locks on memory alone. She gives Rosalind the conductor's role formally—then stays behind to sing a decoy chorus against Serle's hunters. Her song, and her, do not come back. Beat: sacrifice; the torch passed in fire.

chapters.title: The Choir Assembles
chapters.summary: Rosalind, Tam, and Wren—now singing her own true verse—gather the scattered choristers Maren named: a nun, a jailer, a child prodigy. Seven voices. The Codex says the Choir needs eight. Beat: dread arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Eighth Voice
chapters.summary: The only candidate left is Serle. Rosalind offers him not forgiveness but a choice: sing the memories the Regent left him, or stay hollow forever. He weeps and agrees. Beat: mercy as strategy; the enemy's weapon turned.

chapters.title: Under the Palace
chapters.summary: The Choir descends through forgotten ways to the dragon's cavern: a vast, ember-dim creature named Ashvane, who has been singing the kingdom's memory alone for a century and is nearly silent. Beat: scale and sorrow; the world's memory is one tired voice.

chapters.title: Ashvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ashvane can reignite—but only if the Choir carries the kingdom's memories in mortal throats, sharing the dragon's burden. Each singer will hold lifetimes that are not theirs. Rosalind accepts for all of them. Beat: leadership as consent to be changed.

chapters.title: First Rehearsal
chapters.summary: The Choir learns Ashvane's great song; memories flood them—plagues, weddings, a baker's hands, the founding of Thornfell. Tam, who cannot hear, becomes the metronome of the whole. Beat: communion; identity as something shared.

chapters.title: The Regent Descends
chapters.summary: The Regent, feeling the dragon wake, comes down wearing Aldous's body and an army of the forgotten—people it erased, now empty retainers. It offers Rosalind their stolen year back if the Choir stops. Beat: temptation sharpened by the vial's truth.

chapters.title: Rosalind's Refusal
chapters.summary: Rosalind refuses—not for the kingdom, but because a memory returned by the thief is still the thief's. The Regent, wounded by the logic, attacks. The Choir's first defensive chorus shatters the assault. Beat: the theme weaponized; selfhood cannot be gifted by others.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Long Stair
chapters.summary: Retreat up the palace's under-stair, singing as they fight. The child prodigy freezes; Wren throws herself into the breach and is badly hurt—manufactured memory bleeding like real blood. Beat: cost of the found family; courage is chosen, not innate.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Dying, Wren offers her manufactured memories as the eighth voice's fuel—a song built entirely of borrowed life. Rosalind instead sings Wren's own brief, true history: the Choir makes her real by remembering her. Beat: the thesis—identity is what others hold of you.

chapters.title: Wren Remains
chapters.summary: Wren survives, newly, precariously real, and takes the eighth place. Above, the Regent begins eating the city's memory wholesale to power a final assault. Beat: quiet triumph before the storm.

chapters.title: The Silent Night
chapters.summary: The Regent's masterstroke: it erases all sound in the palace. A choir needs to hear itself. Tam, feeling vibration through stone, conducts by touch. Beat: the deaf chorister becomes the spine of the song; disability as mastery.

chapters.title: Crown of Ash
chapters.summary: The Choir reaches the throne room. Rosalind sees the Regent clearly for the first time: it is Ede Voss—or what the crown made of Ede when he tried to control it a century ago. Beat: the author of the prophecy is the monster; inheritance as warning.

chapters.title: Ede's Confession
chapters.summary: The Codex's final pages, sung aloud by Rosalind, reach the Regent: Ede wrote them as instructions for his own unmaking, hidden inside prophecy so the crown couldn't read them. The Regent falters, remembering it was a person. Beat: the plan revealed; grief inside the monster.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: The Choir sings Ede's unbinding while the Regent fights from within, wearing Aldous's screaming face. Rosalind must conduct and hold the king's true name—learned from the vial—simultaneously. Beat: climax begins; every skill and every loss converges.

chapters.title: The Name in the Fire
chapters.summary: Rosalind steps into Ashvane's rekindling flame to carry the king's name at full voice, burning their own memories as fuel. The Regent, unable to eat a song being given rather than kept, unravels into Ede's final, peaceful note. Beat: climax peak; the price made flesh.

chapters.title: Aldous Wakes
chapters.summary: Aldous returns, aged a century in a moment, king of a kingdom that half-remembers him. He recognizes Rosalind—the child from the missing year—and weeps. The crown cools to ordinary gold. Beat: release; the quest's heart answered.

chapters.title: The Kingdom That Doesn't Remember
chapters.summary: The restored memories disperse gently back to their owners. No record of the Choir remains; Rosalind's guild, their deeds, even their name fade from the world's books—only the singers keep them, in each other. Beat: bittersweet cost; invisibility chosen at last.

chapters.title: The New Codex
chapters.summary: Rosalind begins a new book in the Guildhouse, not of prophecy but of record: the Choir's true names, Wren's first real birthday, Maren's songs, Serle's garden. Tam carves the shelf. Beat: healing; memory kept by hand, not magic.

chapters.title: What the Dragon Left
chapters.summary: Ashvane, renewed, offers Rosalind their burned memories back from the dragon's hoard of flame. Rosalind declines some and accepts one: their mother's face, returned at last. Beat: reconciliation with loss; you may choose what you carry.

chapters.title: The Open Road
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Rosalind's POV. The Wayfarers' Guild reopens with the Choir as its first members, carrying memory and goods both. On the first morning, a stranger at the door says, 'I'm told you can help me remember my brother.' Rosalind smiles. 'We can. Come in, and sing.' Beat: full-circle resolution; the silent choir learns its first audience.
